correctness.rationale: Exact face-normal arrangement has six antipodal axes and 32 generic sign chambers, consisting of 20 spherical triangles giving twelve-vertex silhouettes and 12 pentagons giving ten-vertex silhouettes. I independently reconstructed the six normals, generated all 64 sign masks and pair-crossing rays; found exactly the same 32 nonempty chambers (20/12), and checked the first and second weighted moments by fresh 100,000-sphere Monte Carlo. The continuum proof is not the sample: Cauchy brightness W=sum_i |s_i·u|/sqrt(phi+2), spherical Laplacian identities Delta h=-2h and Delta h^2=2|q|^2-6h^2, and constant triangular edge normal and corner values yield exact flux integrals. The complement moments use known E W=3 and absolute-Gaussian two-normal kernel. Checking p>1/(phi+2) proves negative covariance; exceptional directions have spherical measure zero.

originality.rationale: An earlier full-text published Resultary classification of central icosahedron section polygon types establishes exactly the same unweighted 20/12 chamber law and p=15theta/pi-5, which is expressly credited. An earlier full five-Platonic variance result establishes the unconditional dodecahedral E W^2, also credited. The separately published conditional tetrahedral moments use a different normal arrangement. None of these prior statements determines dodecahedral type-weighted first and second moments: marginal silhouette type and unconditional brightness moments lack the joint coupling.
residual_risks: Older stereology tables may include unnoticed type-conditioned dodecahedron moments.
The numerical Monte Carlo tests are not the continuum proof; exact finite chamber construction and spherical integration are required.

value.rationale: How viewing complexity (10 versus 12 vertices) statistically selects projected area is a natural geometric stereology invariant of a highly symmetric convex body. Four exact conditional moments and the rigorous negative area-complexity covariance go beyond known marginal geometry and can support exact conditional variances and sampling analyses.

limitations: Valid only for Haar orthographic views of the regular dodecahedron, almost everywhere.
Does not characterize entire conditional brightness law or arbitrary directions.
